sources.title: Marco Moriggi, Aramaic: introduction, Mnamon, Scuola Normale Superiore
sources.note: Direct full scholarly entry, revised March 2022. Aramaic Script I: 22 consonantal signs, royal court scribes, eighth-century distinction of monumental and cursive hands, Assyrian conquests and later Persian administrative use. Grouped with Examples of writing as one underlying Mnamon Aramaic work.

sources.title: Marco Moriggi, Aramaic: examples of writing, Mnamon
sources.note: Direct full scholarly transcription and translation. Old Aramaic: ninth-century Bar-Hadad stele from Brej north of Aleppo, line 3 unbracketed mlk ʾrm, king of Aram. Official Aramaic I: Bar-Rakib palace inscription, second half of eighth century, loyalty to Tiglath-pileser III and descent from Panammu. Latin scholarly transliteration, not a reconstructed ancient letterform image. Disputed/restored patronymic is omitted. Grouped with Mnamon introduction for cumulative work budget.

sources.title: Deborah Schorsch, Turquoise in Ancient Egypt, Metropolitan Museum of Art (2018)
sources.note: Direct full curatorial scientific essay. Paragraphs beginning Evidence of the exploitation; In Egypt; The Museum has virtually no New Kingdom; The study of light blue-green stones. Mines, tools, habitation and expedition inscriptions; genuine turquoise versus colored glass/faience; XRF elemental sourcing and nonsampling advantage. All language versions and old toah/hd/turqe mirror counted as one work.

sources.title: British Museum, figure of Ramesses II from Serabit el-Khadim, EA697
sources.note: Full indexed museum entry read; direct fetch 403. Curator comments give temple portico findspot, Hathor/turquoise inscriptions, Bintanat on left side and parentage as eldest daughter by Isitnofret. Object is nineteenth dynasty; public date expressed thirteenth century BCE. No claim of ordinary Egyptian family arrangement from royal marriage.

sources.title: Laura Anne Tedesco, Hasanlu in the Iron Age, Metropolitan Museum of Art (2004)
sources.note: Direct full scholarly museum essay: location and route networks, local production, ninth/eighth-century Assyrian influence, Gold Bowl paragraph explicitly no preserved local writing and uncertain ethnic identification. Destruction around 800; Urartian attacker only a hypothesis and not asserted in public copy. Old toah/hd/hslu URL and translations are same work.

sources.title: Robert H. Dyson Jr., The Iron Age Architecture at Hasanlu: An Essay, Expedition 31 (1989)
sources.note: Direct excavator article. Burned Building III kitchen, storerooms, hearth, benches and stairs; Burned Building II artifact distributions identify large jars on first floor and smaller pots along hall bench/shelf. Wall dump contains sheep/goat bones. Group conservatively with Pigott article from same Expedition issue as one publication work.

sources.title: Vincent C. Pigott, The Emergence of Iron Use at Hasanlu, Expedition 31 (1989)
sources.note: Direct research article. Uses of Iron gives over 2000 objects, approximately 90 sickles and 90 small knives; Appearance of Iron Working notes earliest iron not demonstrably mechanically superior to best bronzes. No excavated iron smelting/smithing installation at Hasanlu in report; repair work is an interpretation. Grouped conservatively with Dyson in one 200-word issue allowance.

sources.title: David Stronach, Archaeology II: Median and Achaemenid, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct excavator scholarly overview. Nush-i Jan circa 750 to 550 BCE, four main structures, fire altar and wood-column hall. Ceramics/plant paragraphs give handmade cooking pots, barley, wheats, peas, lentils, grapes; plant sample partly from sixth-century reused settlement. Ethnic identification of individual Median sites remains hazardous. Avoids dated invasion model from opening.

sources.title: Page Selinsky, Lovers, Friends, or Strangers?, Penn Museum Expedition (2017)
sources.note: Direct bioarchaeologist article: Hasanlu destruction around 800 BCE by unidentified invaders; two people found in mudbrick/plaster bin in 1973. One clearly male, second probably male; relationship unknown. Skeletal analysis sections give younger adult without dental disease/old healed injuries and older adult spinal osteoarthritis; no inference of a diagnosed medical service.

proposedOverrides.summary: A mixed atlas label requiring separate regional histories, not one empire.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct contextual card; no aliases. Not merged with arameans, assyria or hittites.
batchIdentityNotes.mapWarning: Identical Sinai and eastern Iraq/western Iran polygons at 1500, 1000 and 700 BCE exclude the Syrian centers. No ancient frontier validation or geometry repair claimed.
batchIdentityNotes.scope: New Kingdom Sinai mining and early Iron Age Iranian sites are regional examples, not Aramaean colonies or one empire. Syrian examples explicitly outside imported polygons. Modern health observation concerns two Hasanlu individuals only.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Verified scholarly Latin transliteration mlk ʾrm, king of Aram, ninth-century Bar-Hadad stele line 3; not reconstructed glyphs. Mnamon introduction and examples grouped as one work.
